previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for bilateral groin pain, which he had been experiencing for one day and which initially improved after his long-standing indwelling Foley catheter was changed in the emergency department. The pain returned with lesser intensity, but there were no signs of active infection such as fever or leukocytosis. Urinalysis showed pyuria and bacteriuria, but repeat testing revealed improvement and the urine culture showed no growth, supporting the conclusion that the findings represented colonization rather than infection. The groin pain and hematuria were attributed to catheter-related trauma. His daughter reported a mechanical fall five days prior with head impact; a non-contrast head CT showed no acute intracranial process. Due to generalized weakness and safety concerns, physical therapy recommended rehabilitation, which the patient accepted after initial hesitation. He was discharged to an extended care facility for physical therapy and close monitoring, with instructions to change his Foley catheter every 4 to 6 weeks and follow up with urology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M w/ BPH and chronic urinary retention, indwelling urinary 
catheter and h/o recurrent multidrug resistant UTIs presenting 
with progressive confusion and groin/suprapubic pain. Found to 
have urinary tract infection, and was treated with IV cefepime 
with clinical improvement. Given patient's deconditioning, he is 
being discharged to rehab.

# Urinary tract infection: Patient with history of recurrent 
multidrug resistant urinary tract infection given his chronic 
indwelling catheter. Urinalysis was grossly positive, so he was 
empirically started on IV cefepime (first day ___ given his 
past culture data. His foley was changed in emergency department 
on ___ when he was admitted. Urine culture grew E. coli that 
was sensitive to cefepime and meropenem. He will finish 10 day 
course of cefepime for complicated urinary tract infection with 
chronic indwelling foley. His last day will be ___. After 
his Cefepime course is done, he should be restarted on his 
Macrobid prophylaxis until he is seen by his urologist, Dr. ___. 
Given patient's continued complaint of intermittent groin pain, 
he was started on detrol to alleviate possible spasms. 

# Pleural effusion/CHF: Patient had chronic left lower lobe 
opacity on admission chest x-ray. His BNP was checked and 
elevated at >1000, and he also developed a new right sided 
pleural effusion on CXR done for comfirmation of PICC placement. 
Itw as thought to be due to volume overload given the fluid he 
received in ED. His last TTE in ___ EF of 50%. So he was 
given 10 mg of IV lasix with good diuresis (net 1 L negative in 
24 hours) and improvement in his clinical status. 

# Anisocoria: On ___, patient's L pupil noted to be larger 
than R in bright light. Pupils almost equalizes in the dim 
light. L pupil sluggishly reactive to light (5->4mm) and R pupil 
briskly reactive to light (4->2mm). No other focal neurological 
findings, no ptosis or impaired extraocular movement. Speech 
fluent, no pronator drift or focal weakness in extremities 
(though limited by patient participation). Given no other focal 
neurological findings, suspicion of ICP or acute stroke low. 
?pseudophakia on exam, but pt denies past surgery. It was 
thought to be due to new anticholinergics (ipratropium), and 
unlikely to be third nerve palsy without ptosis or impaired EOM. 
His ipratropium was discontinued and anisocoria resolved.

# Hypoxia: Per daughter baseline O2 saturations >93% on RA. In 
the past, documented hypoxia down to ~91% on RA on admissions. 
Patient saturating low to mid ___ on 1L NC on admission. 
Initially there was concern for DVT given ___ edema L>R, ___ 
done and negative. Given pleural effusion on second CXR, volume 
overload likely contributing to dyspnea/hypoxia. Patient was 
diuresed with 10 mg IV lasix as above and his respiratory status 
improved. 

# Altered mental status: Patient initially presenting with 
confusion per daughter, who stated he could not recognize her 
and he was only oriented x2. Morning after admission, patient 
was AOx3, but perseverates that he's not feeling well, which was 
similar to how he was doing at home (per daughter). Also 
complaining of generalized weakness. His confusion improved with 
IV antibiotic treatment. 

# Tremors: Per daughter patient has tremors that worsen with 
illness/stresses. In the past, when he was septic/bacteremic, he 
has been tremulous to the point where he could not eat or talk. 
With antibiotic treatment, he improved clinically and his 
facial/hand/feet tremors resolved by the time of discharge. 
 
# Depression: pt was complaining of anxiety, so he was continued 
on home trazadone and citalopram. Per discussion with daughter, 
patient having difficulty dealing with loss of independence in 
the last few months, especially the fact that he needs to go to 
daycare every day. This is also thought to contribute to his 
difficulty going through and working with rehab. Patient may 
benefit in the future from outpatient social worker or 
psychiatric treatment for his depression. 

# Coronary artery disease s/p CABG and stenting x2. Pt had no 
cardiac complaints. He was continued on home dose atorvastatin, 
metroprolol and aspirin.  

# Hypertension: Patient was continued on home metoprolol and 
isosorbide mononitrate with holding parameters. His SBP 
initially decreased to ___ with diuresis, but stabilized in 
100-110s.

# HL: Continued on home atorvastatin.
  
# Diabetes: controlled with diet. Given that diabetes can worsen 
with infection, he was monitored with fingersticks but did not 
require any insulin coverage. So his fingersticks were 
discontinued.

# Constipation: given patient's constipation, his bowel regimen 
was increased. He is being discharged on senna/docusate BID, 
miralax 17 gram daily, dulcolax 10 mg PO/PR BID prn and milk of 
magnesia 30 ml q6 hr prn.

Transitional Issues:
[ ] evaluation and further treatment of his depression and 
anxiety which would hopefully help with further rehab
[ ] further discussion with urology for possible preventative 
measure/prophylaxis for UTI given patient's recurrent UTI. 
[ ] management of constipation - likely worsening in the setting 
of decreased movement/ambulation

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with history of recurrent UTIs, coronary artery
disease status post stenting, hypoxia, chills, altered mental status. 
Evaluate for pneumonia, effusion or pulmonary edema.

COMPARISON:  Multiple chest radiographs, the latest from ___.

TWO VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  The lungs are well expanded and show bilateral
ground-glass and interstitial opacities.  Also noted is a more confluent
opacity in the left lower lobe.  There is a moderate left pleural effusion. 
Sternal wires are intact.  The cardiac silhouette is enlarged.  The
mediastinal silhouette and hilar contours are normal.  No pneumothorax is
present.  Calcified granulomas are noted in the left upper lobe.

IMPRESSION: Left lower lobe opacity with a moderate effusion is unchanged
since ___.  Mild edema.

INDICATION:  Left lower extremity swelling.

TECHNIQUE:  Left lower extremity Doppler sonogram.

COMPARISON:  Ultrasound dated ___.

FINDINGS:  Grayscale and Doppler sonograms of the left common femoral,
superficial femoral, popliteal, and posterior tibial veins were performed. 
There is normal compressibility, flow and augmentation.  The peroneal veins
were not visualized.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of DVT in the left lower extremity.

INDICATION:  PICC positioning.

COMPARISONS:  Chest radiograph from ___.

The new left PICC traverses the expected location of the left brachiocephalic
vein, crosses midline, and terminates in the upper SVC approximately 7 cm
above the expected location of the cavoatrial junction, which was inferred
from a prior chest CT and may not be exact.  

Compared to the study from the prior day, there has been development of a new
moderate right pleural effusion and progression of the pre-existing left
pleural effusion which now opacifies the left lung field up to the level of
the hilum.  The apparent widening of the mediastinum is caused by rotational
differences in the patient position between two studies.  There is no
pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:  New left PICC terminating in the upper SVC.  New moderate right
pleural effusion and possible progression of pre-existing left pleural
effusion.

The position of the PICC was communicated to the IV nurse, ___ via
telephone on ___ at 14:40.  The findings of new pleural effusion
were communicated to Dr. ___ by Dr. ___ via telephone on
___ at 17:00.

INDICATION:  Altered mental status.  History of meningioma.  Evaluation for
acute intracranial changes including hemorrhage or hydrocephalus.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain.  No
contrast was administered.

COMPARISON:  NECT on ___.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, masses, mass effect or
infarction.  A 17 x 10 mm calcified lesion in the left posterior fossa is
again noted, likely representing a calcified meningioma (2a:10).  The
ventricles and sulci are prominent, consistent with age-related atrophy.  No
fractures are identified.  The paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are
clear.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial abnormality.
